notes.he: דת"ק סבר אם שיירו אינו משוייר אלא ירך אמו ודינו כאמו ותנא בתרא סבר אם שיירו לעובר שאם רצה להקדיש לו בפני עצמו לשם זבח אחר היה יכול ולאו ירך אמו הוא ולא הוי דינו כאמו וא"ד איפכא דת"ק סבר אם שיירו משוייר דיכול להקדישו בפני עצמו לחטאת הלכך דינו כחטאת ואידך תנא סבר אם שיירו אינו משוייר:
notes.en: What, is it not that they disagree about this: That the first tanna holds that if he reserved it, it is not reserved, but it is the thigh of its mother and its law is like its mother’s; and the later tanna holds that if he reserved the fetus [it is reserved], so that if he wished to consecrate it on its own for another offering he could, and it is not the thigh of its mother, and its law is not like its mother’s. And some say the reverse: that the first tanna holds that if he reserved it, it is reserved, as he can consecrate it on its own as a sin offering, and therefore its law is like a sin offering; and the other tanna holds that if he reserved it, it is not reserved.

messages.text: Rashi reads this suggestion the other way round: the first tanna holds that if he reserved it, it is reserved, and the second that it is not. Tosafot knows texts that read as printed here and rejects them in favor of Rashi’s reading; Rabbeinu Gershom gives both versions.

Rabbi Yoḥanan could say to you that everyone holds that if he reserved it, it is considered reserved, and therefore a person can consecrate an animal while reserving the fetus as non-sacred. And these tanna’im disagree over this following point: In the case of an animal that was consecrated as a sin offering and only then became pregnant, one Sage holds: The offspring of sacrificial animals become consecrated when they are born and come into being, and as that fetus which was found alive inside the mother was never born, it never became consecrated. And one Sage holds: The offspring of sacrificial animals become consecrated in the womb of their mother, which means that the fetus that was found alive inside the mother was already consecrated.

notes.he: אי בהקדישה מעוברת עסקינן ודאי אם שיירו משוייר וכי לא שיירו קדוש הולד כחטאת גמורה אבל בהקדישה ולבסוף נתעברה פליגי ובהא פליגי דמר סבר בהוייתן ומר סבר במעי אמן:
notes.en: Rabbi Yoḥanan could say to you that everyone: If we are dealing with one who consecrated it while pregnant, certainly if he reserved it, it is reserved, and when he did not reserve it, the offspring is sanctified as a full sin offering. But where he consecrated it and afterward it became pregnant they disagree, and this is what they disagree about: one Sage holds as they come into being, and one Sage holds in their mother’s womb.

messages.text: If you wish, say instead an alternative explanation of the dispute between these two baraitot: It is not difficult for Rabbi Yoḥanan. Everyone holds that if he reserved it, it is considered reserved, and everyone also maintains that offspring of sacrificial animals become consecrated when they are born. Rather, these two baraitot are discussing two different cases. Here, the second baraita is referring to a case where the owner consecrated the animal before it became pregnant and only afterward it became pregnant. Consequently, the offspring is non-sacred, as it was not in the womb when the mother was consecrated, and as it was never born, it was not consecrated at the moment of birth either.

notes.he: ודכ"ע בהוייתן הן קדושין ולא במעי אמן והך דקתני קדוש בחטאת דנתעברה ולבסוף הקדישה דכ"ע אם שיירו משוייר וחשיב למיקדש באנפי נפשיה והני תנאי לא פליגי מידי:
notes.en: Here, where he consecrated it and afterward it became pregnant, etc.: And everyone holds they are sanctified as they come into being and not in their mother’s womb. And the one that teaches that it is sanctified as a sin offering is where it became pregnant and afterward he consecrated it, as everyone holds that if he reserved it, it is reserved, and it is considered fit to be sanctified in its own right; and these tanna’im do not disagree at all.

messages.text: By contrast, there, the first baraita is referring to a case where the animal first became pregnant and afterward the owner consecrated it. Since the owner did not reserve the fetus from the consecration of the mother, the fetus was consecrated as a sin offering together with the mother.

notes.he: הא דמשוי ליה דינו כאמו מיירי דנתעברה ולבסוף הקדיש כיון דהיה יכול להקדיש עובר לחוד ואימיה לחוד יש לו דין חטאת ואידך תנא דלא משוי דינו כחטאת מיירי בהקדישה ולבסוף נתעברה כיון דבשעת הקדש ליכא עובר דמצי מקדיש ליה הלכך לא הוי דינו כאמו:
notes.en: And if you wish, say: They are not difficult. The one that gives it the law of its mother speaks where it became pregnant and afterward he consecrated it: since he could have consecrated the fetus alone and its mother alone, it has the law of a sin offering. And the other tanna, who does not give it the law of a sin offering, speaks where he consecrated it and afterward it became pregnant: since at the time of consecration there was no fetus that he could consecrate, its law is therefore not like its mother’s.

messages.text: From where is it known that the reason for the opinion of Rabbi Yoḥanan is that if he reserved it, it is considered reserved? Perhaps Rabbi Yoḥanan maintains that if he reserved it, it is not considered reserved, and this is the reason for the ruling of Rabbi Yoḥanan: It is that one can achieve atonement with the offspring of a pregnant animal he set aside as a sin offering, as he maintains that a person can achieve atonement with the enhancement of consecrated property, and the fetus is considered an enhancement of consecrated property.

notes.he: אהא דמותבינן ליה לר' יוחנן מאם היתה מעוברת זכתה לו ומוקמינן ליה בתיובתא:
notes.en: Rava objects to this: To that which we raised against Rabbi Yoḥanan from “if she was pregnant, she acquired for him,” and established it as a refutation.

notes.dh: מאן לימא לן דטעמיה דר' יוחנן משום דאם שיירו משוייר
notes.he: דתיהוי תיובתא:
notes.en: Who tells us that Rabbi Yoḥanan’s reason is because if he reserved it, it is reserved: So that it should be a refutation?

notes.he: דאע"ג דמכח אימיה קדיש לא אזיל למיתה דאדם מתכפר בשבח הקדש וכי אזיל ולד חטאת למיתה היכא דלא רצה להתכפר בו אלא באמו:
notes.en: Perhaps Rabbi Yoḥanan’s reason: Is that even though it is sanctified by force of its mother, it does not go to its death, because a person achieves atonement with the enhancement of consecrated property; and the offspring of a sin offering goes to its death where he did not wish to achieve atonement with it but with its mother.

notes.he: [דלמא היינו טעמא דר' יוחנן דאמר רצה בה מתכפר רצה בולד מתכפר דאדם מתכפר בשבח הקדש דהיינו ולד:
notes.en: Perhaps this is the reason of Rabbi Yoḥanan, who said: If he wishes he achieves atonement with it, if he wishes he achieves atonement with its offspring: because a person achieves atonement with the enhancement of consecrated property, which is the offspring.

messages.text: Rabbi Elazar was the pupil of Rabbi Yoḥanan, and he sat before Rabbi Yoḥanan, and Rabbi Elazar assumed that the reason for the opinion of Rabbi Yoḥanan was that he held that if he reserved it, it is considered reserved, and he questioned Rabbi Yoḥanan himself about his statement based on that assumption. And Rabbi Yoḥanan did not answer him with this answer, i.e., that the real reason for his opinion is that a person can achieve atonement with an enhancement of consecrated property.
messages.quote: a person can achieve atonement with the enhancement of consecrated property

notes.he: לא מצית אמרת דטעמיה דרבי יוחנן לאו משום דאם שיירו משוייר דודאי משום הכי הוא דהא רבי אלעזר דאותביה לר' יוחנן לעיל מהיא שלמים וולדה עולה הרי זה ולד שלמים:
notes.en: Rav Hamnuna said to him: You cannot say that Rabbi Yoḥanan’s reason is not because if he reserved it, it is reserved; it is certainly for that reason, as Rabbi Elazar, who objected to Rabbi Yoḥanan above from “it is a peace offering and its offspring a burnt offering, it is the offspring of a peace offering,”

notes.dh: תלמידיה דרבי יוחנן הוא וקמיה הוה יתיב
notes.he: ואותביה ולא אהדר ליה רבי יוחנן האי שינוייא דלימא ליה אנא סבירא לי דמכח אימיה קדוש ולא מחמתיה דנפשיה וטעמא דידי משום דאדם מתכפר בשבח הקדש:
notes.en: was Rabbi Yoḥanan’s student and sat before him: And he objected to him, and Rabbi Yoḥanan did not answer him with this answer, to say to him: I hold that it is sanctified by force of its mother and not on its own account, and my reason is that a person achieves atonement with the enhancement of consecrated property.

notes.dh: א"ל רב המנונא ר' אלעזר תלמיד דר' יוחנן הוה ויתיב קמיה
notes.he: וקא מותיב ליה היא שלמים ולדה עולה (תמורת שלמים דולד):
notes.en: Rav Hamnuna said to him: Rabbi Elazar was a student of Rabbi Yoḥanan and sat before him, and he raised an objection to him from “it is a peace offering and its offspring a burnt offering” (a garbled parenthetical follows in the printed text).

notes.he: אלא א"ל ר' טבלא בר מינה דההיא כו':
notes.en: And he did not answer him with this answer: Rather, Rav Tavla said to him: Apart from this one, etc.

messages.text: And if so, how can you say that the reason for the opinion of Rabbi Yoḥanan is that a person can achieve atonement with the enhancement of consecrated property? Therefore, it must be that the reason for the opinion of Rabbi Yoḥanan is that he held that if he reserved it, it is considered reserved.

notes.dh: ואת אמרת טעמא דר' יוחנן משום דסבר אדם מתכפר בשבח הקדש
notes.he: תימה דהכא משמע דאית ליה לרבי יוחנן אין אדם מתכפר בשבח הקדש ובפ' בתרא דכריתות (דף כז.) מיבעיא ליה ר' אלעזר לר' יוחנן אי מתכפר בשבח הקדש או לא אמר לו כמה [שנים] גדל זה בינינו ועדיין לא ידע אי מתכפר בשבח הקדש או לא אלמא דס"ל דמתכפר וצריך לחלק בין שבח הקדש דתודה לשבח הקדש דחטאת והכא בחטאת:
notes.en: And you say Rabbi Yoḥanan’s reason is because he holds a person achieves atonement with the enhancement of consecrated property: This is puzzling, as here it implies that Rabbi Yoḥanan holds a person does not achieve atonement with the enhancement of consecrated property; yet in the last chapter of Keritot (27a) Rabbi Elazar asked Rabbi Yoḥanan whether one achieves atonement with the enhancement of consecrated property or not, and he said to him: How many [years] has this one grown up among us, and he still does not know whether one achieves atonement with the enhancement of consecrated property or not! Evidently he holds that one does. One must distinguish between the enhancement of consecrated property in a thanks offering and the enhancement of consecrated property in a sin offering, and here it is a sin offering.

notes.he: אלא מדלא אהדר ליה הכי ש"מ דטעם דר' יוחנן משום דאם שיירו משוייר הוא:
notes.en: And you say, etc.: Rather, since he did not answer him so, learn from it that Rabbi Yoḥanan’s reason is because if he reserved it, it is reserved.

messages.text: The mishna teaches: And if it was only after he said: This animal is hereby a peace offering, that he reconsidered and said: Its offspring is a burnt offering, that offspring is a peace offering, as before he reconsidered the offspring had already assumed the status of the offspring of a peace offering.
messages.quote: after he said: This animal is hereby a peace offering, that he reconsidered

messages.text: If he reconsidered after saying: This animal is a peace offering, it is obvious that he cannot remove the status he already applied to the animal, and that the offspring remains a peace offering. Can one change his mind anytime that he wants?

notes.he: בתמיה:
notes.en: Can one change his mind anytime that he wants: [Said] in astonishment.

messages.text: This halakha is necessary only in a case where he reconsidered and said: Its offspring is a burnt offering, within the time required for speaking a short phrase. Lest you say: The halakhic status of a pause that lasts less than the time required for speaking a short phrase is like that of continuous speech, and therefore the offspring is a burnt offering, and that time he was merely prolonging his thought but not changing his mind; consequently, the mishna teaches us that he changed his mind and it is not considered continuous speech.
messages.quote: Can one change his mind anytime that he wants?

notes.he: כדי שאלת שלום רב לתלמיד ואמרי לה תלמיד לרב (ב"ק עג:):
notes.en: Within the time required for speaking: The time of a teacher’s greeting to a student; and some say, of a student to a teacher (Bava Kamma 73b).

notes.dh: לא נצרכה שאמר תוך כדי דיבור
notes.he: פי' כדי שאלת [שלום] תלמיד לרב שלום עליך רבי דהא דקיי"ל (ב"ב קכ:) תוך כדי דיבור כדיבור דמי והיינו כדי שאלת רב לתלמיד:
notes.en: It is necessary only where he said it within the time required for speaking: Meaning, the time of a student’s greeting to a teacher, “Peace be upon you, my teacher”; for that which we hold (Bava Batra 120b), that within the time required for speaking is like speaking, that is the time of a teacher’s greeting to a student.

messages.text: Mishna

If one had two animals standing before him, one a burnt offering and the other a peace offering, and he said with regard to a third, non-sacred animal: This animal is hereby the substitute of the burnt offering, the substitute of the peace offering,

that animal is the substitute of the burnt offering. This is the statement of Rabbi Meir. Once he designated it as the substitute of the burnt offering, his initial statement takes effect and the animal assumes the sanctity of the burnt offering.

notes.he: דר"מ אית ליה תפוס לשון ראשון:
notes.en: MISHNA: This is the substitute of a burnt offering: For Rabbi Meir holds “grasp the first expression.”

notes.dh: מתני' ה"ז תמורת עולה ותמורת שלמים ה"ז תמורת עולה דברי ר"מ
notes.he: דקסבר תפוס לשון ראשון:
notes.en: MISHNA: This is the substitute of a burnt offering and the substitute of a peace offering; this is the substitute of a burnt offering, the statement of Rabbi Meir: For he holds “grasp the first expression.”

messages.text: If that was his intent from the outset, when he said that the animal is the substitute of the burnt offering, to state that the animal is also the substitute of the peace offering, then since it is impossible to call two designations simultaneously, i.e., one must first say one designation and then the other, his statement stands, and the animal is half a burnt offering and half a peace offering.

notes.he: וחציה תמורת עולה וחציה תמורת שלמים ותרעה עד שתסתאב ותמכר ויביא בדמי חציה תמורת עולה ובדמי חציה תמורת שלמים. ובהכי עסקינן שהיו לפניו עולה ושלמים כשהמיר את זו בהן:
notes.en: His statement stands: And half of it is the substitute of a burnt offering and half the substitute of a peace offering, and it grazes until it becomes blemished and is sold, and with the money of half of it he brings [an offering for] the substitute of a burnt offering, and with the money of half [an offering for] the substitute of a peace offering. And we are dealing here with a case where a burnt offering and a peace offering were before him when he substituted this one for them.

notes.dh: ר' יוסי אומר אם לכן נתכוון מתחלה
notes.he: שתהא תמורת שניהם אע"ג דלא אמר ה"ז תמורת עולה ושלמים אלא אמר ה"ז תמורת עולה (ותמורת שלמים) [ושלמים] הואיל ואי אפשר כו' דבריו קיימין ותימכר ויביא בדמיה חציה תמורת עולה ובחציין תמורת שלמים:
notes.en: Rabbi Yosei says: If that was his intent at first, that it be the substitute of both, even though he did not say “this is the substitute of a burnt offering and a peace offering” but said “this is the substitute of a burnt offering (and the substitute of a peace offering) [and a peace offering]” [the printed text corrects itself here and the clause is unclear], since it is impossible, etc., his statement stands; and it is sold, and with half its money he brings the substitute of a burnt offering and with half the substitute of a peace offering.

messages.text: And if it was only after he said: This animal is hereby the substitute of the burnt offering, that he reconsidered and said: The substitute of the peace offering, that entire animal is the substitute of the burnt offering.

notes.dh: אם משאמר תמורת עולה ואחר כך נמלך ואמר כו'
notes.he: הרי זו תמורת עולה בלבד תרוייהו קדשי. ותמכר ותביא בדמי חציה תמורת עולה ובדמי חציה תמורת שלמים:
notes.en: If after he said “the substitute of a burnt offering” he afterward reconsidered and said, etc.: It is the substitute of a burnt offering only. Both are sanctified, and it is sold, and with the money of half of it he brings the substitute of a burnt offering and with the money of half the substitute of a peace offering. [So the printed text.]

messages.caption: The two mishnayot on this daf: what takes effect when one says two designations one after the other, according to Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yosei.

messages.text: Continues on 26a: the Gemara on this mishna, where Rabbi Yitzḥak, son of Rabbi Yosei, says in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan that everyone concedes when one says the substitute of a burnt offering will take effect and afterward the substitute of a peace offering.
